edits.new: Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post. Use ancestors and descendants to interpret the selected sense and level of abstraction. Distinguish defining alternatives or jointly required parts from illustrative details. Preserve every defining part and the restrictions applying to it. A description requiring several parts together may narrow the topic of a required part; the other parts need not be instances of that part's kind or action. Decide whether the defining parts are required together or admitted independently; co-mention alone does not settle this. If a coherent interpretation cannot be justified, record the ambiguity as unresolved.
edits.old: Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post. Preserve all explicitly named alternatives and parts. Use ancestors and descendants to help interpret its sense and level of abstraction. Do not apply every ancestor restriction automatically or discard any named alternative or required part to make a relationship fit. A description requiring several parts together may narrow the topic of a required part; the other parts need not be instances of that part's kind or action. Decide whether multiple named parts must be described together or are alternatives admitted independently. Co-mention alone does not settle this. Preserve the restrictions the selected subject applies to each admitted alternative. If a coherent interpretation of the selected subject cannot be justified, record the ambiguity as unresolved.

edits.new: Write `meaning` from the chosen membership conditions. Express the general condition itself; keep illustrative members and explanations of rejected restrictions in `resolutions`, even when supplied by the selected subject.
edits.old: Use the conditions chosen in `resolutions` when writing `meaning`. Keep explanations of rejected restrictions in `resolutions`.

edits.new: Derive `title` solely from finalized `meaning`. Name what the meaning defines: an object, a person, an activity, a plan or another topic. Preserve that referent and its roles in a brief, natural name. An action describing an object does not make that action the topic. For a plan or preference, name its stated goal rather than enumerating the actions serving it. Leave exact scope and qualifications in `meaning`; the title need not reproduce them. Use a broader familiar name when it preserves recognizable identity. Do not change `meaning` to fit the title. If `meaning` is null, `title` must be null.
edits.old: Derive `title` solely from finalized `meaning`. Give its central topic a brief, natural name that denotes the same kind of thing and preserves the same roles. For a plan or preference involving several actions toward one stated goal, name the plan or preference by that goal. Leave steps, exact scope and qualifications in `meaning`. A broader familiar name may improve clarity while preserving that topic's identity. Do not change `meaning` to fit the title. If `meaning` is null, `title` must be null.
